To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the rates of mineralisation of organic compounds in natural waters are directly proportional to the concentrations of the organic compounds and are affected by the nutrient supply.
the rate of phenol mineralisation in lake water is directly related to the nutrient concentration in the water.
the rate of phenol mineralisation in samples from three lakes was directly proportional to the phenol concentration and the trophic status of the water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of nutrients on the mineralization of organic pollutants in the aquatic environment.
the effect of environmental conditions on the rate of microbial degradation of organic compounds.
the effect of nutrient levels on the rates of microbial mineralization of trace organic compounds in natural waters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rates of mineralizatio n of phenol and nitrophenol were affected by the concentration of the substrate, the nutrient status of the sample, and the source of the sample.
nutrient limitation of the rate of mineralized phenol in lake and stream water is a function of the trophic state of the water and the concentration of phenol.
nutrient levels in natural waters are important determinants in the rate of mineralisation of trace concentrations of organic compounds.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the rate of mineralizaton of phenol in natural waters is directly proportional to the concentration of phenol, the rate is dependent on the nutrient status of the water, and the rate is affected by the presence of nutrients.
inorganic nutrients, amino acids, and yeast extract stimulate the rate of phenol and/or p-nitro phenol mineralization at trace concentrations in water samples.
the rates of mineralisation of phenol and 2-nitrophenols are directly related to the concentration of the substrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nutrient limitation of microbial processes can be a significant control on the fate of organic compounds.
nutrient concentrations affect mineralization rates of organic compounds in natural water.
nutrients in the environment can influence the rate of degradation of organic contaminants.
